answer: Here is one mechanism that works: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because ember only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, beacon is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any gale approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
